description: The District-scale Resilience Benchmark Dataset, published by the uvicjames repository maintainer, supplies infrastructure network representations for district-level resilience research. The README names synthetic networks and place-based examples in Jamestown and Frewsburg, New York, Silver Firs in Washington and Mirvish Village in Toronto. Model 1 contains water and electricity networks constructed from a Jamestown street layout, plus physical dependencies between their nodes. File metadata identifies GraphML networks, XML geometry and dependency descriptions, OBJ geometry, terrain TIFF files and SVG diagrams. These public files are provided through GitHub under the repository's MIT licence, free of charge. Coverage and detail vary by model; the documentation does not establish a common observation period or validated asset-level accuracy. The README lists ten models, while the current directory tree contains nine and lacks M5. It also labels the collection as work in progress. Model 1 warns that network heights do not snap to terrain and that most geometry is centred around the origin while terrain retains its original coordinates. The inputs can support controlled network and interdependency experiments. They complement IN-CORE (platform-in-core) as research testbeds; format compatibility was not tested.
